body.text:
1 śrāvastyāṃ nidānam /
2 ye kecid bhikṣavaḥ samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajaṃti sarve te caturṇām ā

children.text:
satyānāṃ jñānāya /
3 katameṣāṃ caturṇām /
4 duḥkham āryasatyasya duḥkhasamudayasya duḥkhanirodhasya duḥkha
children.translated_text:
truths.
3. Which four?
4. The noble truth of suffering, of the origin of suffering, of the cessation of suffering, of the

children.text:
odhagāminī pratipad āryasatyasya jñānāya /
5 tasmāt tarhi caturṇām āryasatyānām anabhisamitānām abhisamayāya atimātraṃ tīvra
children.translated_text:
sation-of-suffering-leading path — for the knowledge of this noble truth.
5. Therefore, for the realization of the four noble truths not yet realized, extremely intense

children.text: ndo vyāyāmaś cotsuḍhiś cāprativāṇiś ca smṛtyā saṃprajanyena ca yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: sire, exertion, enthusiasm, and non-retreat should be practiced with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension).

children.text: MS "abhisamayāya adhimātra tivraś ca vyāyāmaś" for "abhisamayāya adhimātraṃ tīvraś chandaś ca vyāyāmaś"?

6. Which four?
7. The noble truth of suffering — the noble
the path leading to the cessation of suffering —

children.text:
tyasūtraṃ samāptaḥ /
9 rakṣaṃ bhavatu // + + + syasya svāhā //
children.translated_text:
<s>sūtra</s> is completed.
9. May there be protection! ... <s>svāhā</s>!

body.translated_text:
